## ai.proxy runtimes: how each harness consumes the resolved endpoint

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-14 — Claude's settings-file delivery and Codex's
> provider (user config.toml on Home Manager, launcher session flags on devenv)
> render from `resolvedProxy` through one renderer each (`ai-proxy.md`). Kimchi,
> Kiro and Copilot omit `proxy` from `surfaceSupport` and warn through the
> generated warning cases.

### Claude (packages/claude-code/lib/proxy.nix)

Claude has no launcher, and a settings `env` beats the process env, so the
endpoint travels only through settings files. `render` writes
`env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (the origin; Claude appends `/v1/messages`) and BOTH
key methods, the unused one blank: `env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` for `plain`,
`apiKeyHelper` for `file` (coreutils `cat <path>`) or `helper`. Settings merge
per key across scopes, so a key method left set in a lower scope would also be
sent to this proxy. `env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is written blank, never with a
value: interactive Claude asks before using a value, and declining sends the
claude.ai login to the proxy; left unset, one inherited from the process env or
another scope is sent to the proxy as `x-api-key` beside the proxy key (probed
on Claude Code 2.1.296: the blank suppresses it for both key methods, with no
prompt). Any selection also sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` and
`DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` at `mkDefault`.

Where each form lands:

- An endpoint (`url` on either backend, or a Home Manager `instance`):
  `native.settings`, so the settings.json the backend already writes. The proxy
  leaves are at ordinary priority, so a consumer's own value for one is a
  definition conflict.
- `instance`, devenv: `.claude/settings.local.json`, the highest file scope,
  rendered at shell entry. Claude saves permission answers there, so it is a
  reconciled `shared` document: only the proxy leaves are owned, and they are
  retracted when the selection goes. Until its ledger exists, the renderer fails
  on a proxy leaf someone else already put in the file instead of replacing it.

For devenv's `instance`, a consumer's `native.settings` value for a proxy leaf
fails an assertion. The `claudeProxySettings` writer is declared with
`runWhenDisabled`, so dropping the selection or disabling Claude retracts its
output.

### Codex (`packages/chatgpt-codex/lib/proxy.nix`)

One provider table per endpoint: `base_url` is the origin plus `/v1`, `name` is
the provider id (Codex refuses to load a provider without one),
`wire_api = "responses"` and `requires_openai_auth = false`. `true` would send a
ChatGPT login's token to the proxy. `plain` becomes `experimental_bearer_token`.
`file` and `helper` become command-backed `auth` (`cat <path>`, or the helper),
which Codex re-runs every five minutes and after a 401. Never `env_key`: tool
subprocesses inherit it, and Home Manager's launcher environment does not reach
devenv's.

- **Home Manager** writes `model_provider = "ai-proxy"` and
  `[model_providers.ai-proxy]` into user config.toml, plus the overridable
  defaults `features.plugins = false` and `analytics.enabled = false`, which
  stop plugin sync and usage metrics from reaching other hosts. A devenv shell
  inherits the user file with no devenv configuration.
- **devenv** cannot use project config: Codex strips `model_provider` and
  `model_providers` from project layers. Its launcher passes
  `-c model_providers.ai-proxy-devenv={…}` and
  `-c model_provider=ai-proxy-devenv`, the highest layer. The `url` form is
  baked in as `--add-flag`s. The `instance` form runs `ai-proxy-render --lines`
  at each launch, and a failed lookup aborts the launch. The quieting defaults
  go to the trusted project's config.toml.
- **A separate id on devenv is load-bearing.** Codex deep-merges layers per key,
  so session flags reusing `ai-proxy` would add their auth fields to the user
  table, and `auth` beside `experimental_bearer_token` fails to load.
- No `[profiles.*]` or `profile`: the pinned Codex rejects both.

`chatgpt-codex-proxy` runs the pinned binary against loopback mock proxies in
the build sandbox. It covers each Home Manager key form, both devenv forms, Home
Manager plus devenv with different key forms, and a missing instance aborting
the launch.

### Kimchi, Kiro, Copilot

Kimchi and Kiro are deferred. They receive the standard unsupported-surface
warning, not a silent drop. Copilot is out of scope and warns the same way.
`ai-warnings-delivery` generates those cases from the records on both backends.
Research and the per-harness permutation map are operator working files, outside
the repository.

### Checks

`packages/claude-code/checks/claude-proxy.nix` covers Claude: key forms,
precedence, the override, a Home Manager `instance` in settings.json, the devenv
renderer executed, and the real devenv writer across shell entries.
`packages/chatgpt-codex/checks/chatgpt-codex-proxy.nix` holds the Codex checks.
